Meta Muse vs Hermes is the comparison I care about most, because Hermes Agent is what I run my business on. Both are free to start. Muse is Meta’s managed, polished personal agent; Hermes is open source, runs on your own machine, and uses any model you choose. Interestingly, Muse borrows ideas Hermes users already know — memory and persona files — and puts a friendly interface on them. The video above shows my Hermes Agent OS. Here’s the honest comparison.

Key takeaways

- Both free to start — Muse via Meta’s free tier, Hermes because it’s open source.

- Control: Hermes gives you the model choice, the data and the code; Muse keeps everything on Meta’s cloud.

- Ease: Muse is ready in minutes; Hermes takes setup but goes much further.

- Privacy: Hermes can run fully locally; with Muse, your tasks run on Meta’s servers.

items.title: Meta Muse: Meta’s AI Agent Explained (2026)
items.content:
Meta Muse is Meta’s personal AI agent — launched on 8 September 2026, free to start, and quickly the top app in the App Store. It doesn’t just chat: it books travel, fills in forms, tracks prices, negotiates bills and checks out for you, from its own app or inside WhatsApp. It runs on Muse Spark 1.3, the model family I covered back in April (video above). Here’s what Muse actually is, what it costs, how it keeps your accounts safe, where it falls short — and how it stacks up against the agents I test every week.

Key takeaways

- What it is: an always-on personal agent with its own cloud computer, available in its own app, on the web and through WhatsApp — US-first.

- Price: free tier with up to 100M tokens a week, then Power at $20/month and Maximum at $100/month.

- Safety design: an isolated Secure VM, a separate Sentinel guard agent, a credential vault the agent can’t read, approvals for critical actions and a full activity log.

- Best for: non-technical users and everyday life admin. For coding, building and business automation, other agents are stronger.

## What Meta Muse actually does

Muse is built for personal tasks more than technical work. You give it a goal — book a trip, cancel a subscription, sell something on Marketplace, find a cheaper bill — and it works through the steps on its own cloud computer, checking in when something needs your approval. It connects to Gmail, Google Calendar, OpenTable, Facebook, Instagram, Peloton and Plaid, pays with one-time cards through Link by Stripe, and can make proactive suggestions, like turning saved recipes into a grocery list.

Reviewers consistently praise the interface. According to Nate Herk’s hands-on comparison, Muse gives you an approvals tab, a schedule tab, a heartbeat that checks your documents and email every 30 minutes, goals and ideas sections, a customisable feed, and even generated podcasts — plus an identity tab where you can read and edit the agent’s memory and persona files. If you’ve set up Hermes or OpenClaw, that last part will feel familiar; Muse just makes it visual.

## Meta Muse pricing and the safety model

  • Interface: Muse has a full app; Instinct works through text — its own iMessage line, plus an inbox and calls.
